# MCP Command Reference

The `caliper-mcp` server exposes every agent-enabled command in `src/builder/commands/command_table.json` as one Model Context Protocol tool.
The script `scripts/generate_mcp_reference.py` generates this page directly from `src/builder/commands/command_table.json`.
Continuous integration runs `python scripts/generate_mcp_reference.py --check` and fails when this page drifts from the command table.
After any edit to `src/builder/commands/command_table.cpp`, run `caliper_builder_command_table --write` and then run `python3 scripts/generate_mcp_reference.py --write`.

## Tool Mapping and Execution

Each command with `agents: true` becomes one MCP tool whose name replaces the first dot with an underscore.
For example, `panel.create` becomes `panel_create`, while its MCP `title` keeps the dotted command name.
The tool input schema matches the command `args` schema, and the structured output schema matches `result`.
Commands that return `png_base64` (`capture_frame` and `panel_render`) return MCP `image/png` content alongside the JSON metadata.
The server marks a tool with `readOnlyHint: true` only when `mutates` is false, `effect` is not `run`, and the command is not `app.launch`.
See [MCP Server](../agents/mcp-server.md) and [Caliper API](../agents/http-api.md) for transport, token, and approval rules.

## Application Commands

Application commands inspect host versions, list instruments, and switch the active instrument.

| MCP Tool | Command | Effect | Flags | Arguments | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `app_info` | `app.info` | `read` | `read-only` | None | Describes the running Caliper app: its version, the ABI epoch its instrument libraries must be built for, the services it offers, and the versions of the SDK, libtorch and its interface libraries. It changes nothing. |
| `app_instruments` | `app.instruments` | `read` | `read-only`, `frame-thread` | None | Lists the instruments the app found, as caliper list shows them: each instrument's manifest id, its version, its kind (library or spec), its folder, its status (READY, ACTIVE for the one open now, REFUSED, SHADOWED) and the reason when it cannot run. The id is what app.launch takes. It changes nothing. |
| `app_launch` | `app.launch` | `change` | `frame-thread` | `id` (string, required) | Opens the page of one instrument, as a click on its row on the app's landing screen does; an attached live session stays attached. The id is an instrument's manifest id from app.instruments. An instrument with a library replaces the page shown at once. An instrument written as a spec in the workspace opens with an instrument.open from your origin, and the page changes only when that has run: when it would replace the open spec's unsaved changes it waits for the person's approval, the status is PENDING_APPROVAL rather than ACTIVE, its note says how to check whether it opened, and if the person denies it nothing changes. |

## Catalog Commands

Catalog commands list, describe, and sample data sources across workspace stores and live feeds.

| MCP Tool | Command | Effect | Flags | Arguments | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `catalog_list` | `catalog.list` | `read` | `read-only` | `kind` (enum), `limit` (integer), `prefix` (string) | Lists the sources in the catalog: every table, tensor, live view, feed channel and metric that a spec can bind, with its schema, shape and rate. A source id is &lt;kind&gt;:&lt;name&gt;, such as table:run42_metrics or live:attn.weights; a spec source names it in its catalog field. Filter by kind or by the start of the name. It changes nothing. |
| `catalog_describe` | `catalog.describe` | `read` | `read-only` | `id` (string, required) | Gives one catalog source in full: its kind, where it comes from, its columns and row count for a table, feed or metric, its dtype and shape for a tensor or live view, its rate, its size, whether it can run in the browser viewer, and any warnings. The id comes from catalog.list. |
| `catalog_sample` | `catalog.sample` | `read` | `read-only` | `count` (array), `id` (string, required), `limit` (integer), `start` (array) | Shows a little of a source's data, to learn what it holds before binding it. A table, feed or metric gives up to limit rows (20 by default). A tensor or live view gives its statistics (min, max, mean, standard deviation and the count of non-finite values) and a box of its values, at most 64 per axis and 4096 in all, placed with start and count. The id comes from catalog.list. It changes nothing. |

## Data Store Commands

Data store commands run read-only SQL queries and import tabular files into the workspace store.

| MCP Tool | Command | Effect | Flags | Arguments | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data_query` | `data.query` | `read` | `read-only` | `limit` (integer), `sql` (string, required), `timeout_ms` (integer) | Runs one read-only SQL SELECT, in DuckDB's dialect, over the workspace's tables, which are the table: sources of the catalog named without the table: prefix. It returns at most limit rows (1000 by default) and stops after timeout_ms (5000 by default). Use it to explore data or to try the SQL of a spec source. It changes nothing. |
| `data_import` | `data.import` | `change` | `mutates` | `paths` (array, required), `run` (boolean) | Creates a loader for each file path given, choosing the reader from the file's extension (csv, tsv, parquet, json, jsonl, arrow, npy, npz, safetensors, hdf5, png, jpg, wav), and runs the new loaders unless run is false, so that the files' contents appear in the catalog as table: and tensor: sources. Paths are relative to the workspace; a path outside it is accepted only from the person's own drop or file dialog. Pickle files are refused. Undo deletes the loaders it created and their outputs. |

## Loader Commands

Loader commands manage and execute workspace file and Python data loaders.

| MCP Tool | Command | Effect | Flags | Arguments | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `loader_list` | `loader.list` | `read` | `read-only` | None | Lists the workspace's saved loaders. A loader is a saved recipe that turns files into catalog sources: a file or glob, a reader, and optional SQL or tensor transforms. Each has an id, which the other loader commands take. It changes nothing. |
| `loader_describe` | `loader.describe` | `read` | `read-only` | `id` (string, required) | Gives one loader in full: its TOML recipe, its reader and input path, how its last run went and the catalog sources it made. The id comes from loader.list. |
| `loader_create` | `loader.create` | `change` | `mutates` | `run` (boolean), `text` (string, required) | Saves a new loader from its TOML recipe, as loaders/&lt;id&gt;.loader.toml in the workspace, and runs it when run is true. The recipe holds caliper_loader = 0; a [loader] table with id and title; an [input] table with path (a file or glob relative to the workspace) and an optional reader; optional [reader] options; and one or more [[output]] tables, each with a name and an optional SQL SELECT over the relation input, or a tensor to select. It fails when a loader with that id exists. Undo deletes it. |
| `loader_update` | `loader.update` | `change` | `mutates`, `destructive` | `id` (string, required), `run` (boolean), `text` (string, required) | Replaces the recipe of an existing loader with new TOML text, whose [loader] id must stay the same, and runs it when run is true. It overwrites the saved recipe, so an agent's call needs the person's approval. Undo restores the previous recipe; the tables the new recipe made stay until the loader runs again. The id comes from loader.list. |
| `loader_run` | `loader.run` | `change` | `mutates`, `destructive` | `id` (string, required) | Runs a loader: reads its input files and rebuilds its outputs, which replaces the tables and tensors its previous run made. A Python loader runs as a separate process. This cannot be undone, and an agent's call needs the person's approval. The id comes from loader.list. |
| `loader_delete` | `loader.delete` | `change` | `mutates`, `destructive` | `id` (string, required), `keep_outputs` (boolean) | Deletes a saved loader and, unless keep_outputs is true, the catalog sources it made. An agent's call needs the person's approval. Undo restores the recipe; its outputs come back when it runs again. The id comes from loader.list. |

## Spec Document Commands

Spec document commands create, open, read, replace, and validate the active spec document.

| MCP Tool | Command | Effect | Flags | Arguments | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `spec_new` | `spec.new` | `change` | `mutates`, `frame-thread` | `description` (string), `id` (string, required), `layout_locked` (boolean), `title` (string) | Starts a new, empty spec and makes it the open spec: the one the builder shows and that the source, panel and layout commands edit. A spec is the text that describes an instrument built from data: its sources, its panels and their layout. The id names the instrument, in lower case with digits, - and _. Undo returns to the spec that was open before. |
| `spec_open` | `spec.open` | `change` | `mutates`, `frame-thread` | `path` (string, required) | Opens a spec file of the workspace as the open spec. The path is relative to the workspace and ends in .spec.toml, such as instruments/attention-entropy/attention-entropy.spec.toml. To open a saved instrument by its id, use instrument.open. Undo returns to the spec that was open before, with its unsaved changes. |
| `spec_get` | `spec.get` | `read` | `read-only`, `frame-thread` | `instrument` (string) | Returns the open spec as its TOML text and as its canonical JSON form, with its instrument id, the file it was saved to or opened from, and whether it has unsaved changes. With instrument, it returns that saved instrument's spec instead, read from its files without opening it. When no spec is open and no instrument is named, it answers open false and nothing else, which is not an error: make one with spec.new or open one with spec.open or instrument.open. It changes nothing. |
| `spec_set_text` | `spec.set_text` | `edit` | `mutates`, `frame-thread` | `dry_run` (boolean), `text` (string, required) | Replaces the whole open spec with new TOML text after checking it; text with an error is refused, and the open spec stays as it was. Use spec.validate first to see every error. Undo restores the previous text. The result holds the change as a diff; with dry_run true the change is only checked and not applied. |
| `spec_validate` | `spec.validate` | `read` | `read-only`, `frame-thread` | `text` (string) | Checks a spec and lists its errors and warnings, each with a code, a message and where it is. It checks the given text, or the open spec when no text is given. An invalid spec is reported in the result, not as an error. It changes nothing. |

## Source Commands

Source commands add, patch, and remove data sources and transform chains in the active spec.

| MCP Tool | Command | Effect | Flags | Arguments | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source_add` | `source.add` | `edit` | `mutates`, `frame-thread` | `catalog` (string), `dry_run` (boolean), `from` (string), `history` (integer), `id` (string, required), `sql` (string), `transform` (array) | Adds a source to the open spec. A spec source gives data a name that panels bind. It has exactly one of catalog (a catalog source id from catalog.list, such as live:attn.weights), sql (one read-only SELECT over the workspace's tables) or from (the id of another source of this spec), and an optional list of tensor transforms (slice, reduce, normalise) for tensor-shaped data. Undo removes it. The result holds the change as a diff; with dry_run true the change is only checked and not applied. |
| `source_patch` | `source.patch` | `edit` | `mutates`, `frame-thread` | `dry_run` (boolean), `id` (string, required), `patch` (object, required) | Changes a source of the open spec with a JSON merge patch (RFC 7386): the keys given replace the source's own, and a key set to null is removed. The id cannot change. The id comes from spec.get. Undo restores the source. The result holds the change as a diff; with dry_run true the change is only checked and not applied. |
| `source_remove` | `source.remove` | `edit` | `mutates`, `frame-thread` | `dry_run` (boolean), `id` (string, required) | Removes a source from the open spec. A source that a panel binds, or that another source derives from, cannot be removed until they change. The id comes from spec.get. Undo restores it. The result holds the change as a diff; with dry_run true the change is only checked and not applied. |

A panel draws one primitive from the sources it binds: series (lines), heatmap (a colour-mapped grid), points (a 2-D or 3-D cloud), histogram, table, image or text. bind maps each slot of the primitive to a spec source id, or to &lt;source&gt;.&lt;column&gt; for one column of a tabular source. place puts it beside, above, below or in tabs with another panel; without place, the panel goes to the right of the whole layout. The result holds the change as a diff; with dry_run true the change is only checked and not applied. |
| `panel_render` | `panel.render` | `read` | `read-only`, `frame-thread`, `png-image` | `height` (integer), `id` (string, required), `width` (integer) | Draws one panel of the open spec off screen and returns it as a PNG image, so that you can check what it looks like. width and height are in pixels, 800 by 500 by default. The id comes from spec.get. It changes nothing. |
| `panel_data` | `panel.data` | `read` | `read-only`, `frame-thread` | `instrument` (string), `known` (string), `panel` (string, required) | Returns the data of one panel as the browser viewer draws it: the panel's data after its sources' transforms, within the bounds of what a panel can show (long lines as a min/max envelope, large grids and clouds sampled at a stride, a histogram's bin counts, the first 1,000 rows of a table), with a version. Pass the version you have as known, and the answer is unchanged, with no data, until the panel's sources, the spec or the catalog change. It reads a saved instrument with instrument, else the open spec. It changes nothing. |

## Layout Commands

Layout commands place panels, set split trees and shares, and lock or unlock the layout.

| MCP Tool | Command | Effect | Flags | Arguments | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `layout_place` | `layout.place` | `edit` | `mutates`, `frame-thread` | `dry_run` (boolean), `panel` (string, required), `ratio` (number), `target` (string, required), `where` (enum, required) | Places a panel of the open spec next to another one, the target: beside puts it to the right, above and below above or below, tabbed in tabs with the target. ratio is the share of the space the placed panel gets, from 0.05 to 0.95, half by default. A panel already in the layout is moved. Undo restores the previous layout. The result holds the change as a diff; with dry_run true the change is only checked and not applied. |
| `layout_set` | `layout.set` | `edit` | `mutates`, `frame-thread` | `dry_run` (boolean), `layout` (object, required) | Replaces the whole layout of the open spec. The layout is a flat list of nodes: each node splits its space horizontally or vertically between its children, with ratio the share of the first child or shares one share for each child, or shows them in tabs; mins gives a panel or control child its minimum in columns and lines. A child is a panel id or another node's id, and root names the top node, or the one panel when there is only one. Every panel of the spec should appear once; a panel left out is not drawn. Undo restores the previous layout. The result holds the change as a diff; with dry_run true the change is only checked and not applied. |
| `layout_lock` | `layout.lock` | `edit` | `mutates`, `frame-thread` | `dry_run` (boolean), `locked` (boolean, required) | Locks or unlocks the open spec's whole layout. While locked, every panel and control is non-closable and layout edits (adding, removing, moving or replacing components) are refused with layout.locked until unlocked. Undo restores the previous lock state. The result holds the change as a diff; with dry_run true the change is only checked and not applied. |

## Preview Commands

Preview commands stage, diff, commit, or discard multi-step spec edits before workspace mutation.

| MCP Tool | Command | Effect | Flags | Arguments | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `preview_begin` | `preview.begin` | `read` | `read-only`, `frame-thread` | `id` (string), `panel` (string), `source` (string) | Starts a preview of the open spec: a scratch copy on which edits of the open spec stack, each checked like a real edit, while the open spec, the undo history and the journal stay as they are. An edit reaches the preview when its call names the preview's id, which Caliper API takes in the X-Caliper-Preview header; spec.get, spec.validate and panel.render read the preview the same way. With panel or source the preview is scoped to that target: its edits may change only the target, the sources a target panel binds and the items the preview adds. preview.diff shows the stacked change, and only the person commits it, with Accept in Caliper. A preview ends when it is committed or discarded, or after 30 minutes without use. |
| `preview_diff` | `preview.diff` | `read` | `read-only`, `frame-thread` | `id` (string, required) | Shows what a preview would change: the diff of the open spec's canonical TOML against the preview with every edit stacked on it, how many edits it holds and what the validator warns about. When the open spec changed since the edits were made, they are applied to it again first, and when one no longer applies the call fails with history.conflict. It changes nothing. |
| `preview_commit` | `preview.commit` | `edit` | `mutates`, `frame-thread` | `id` (string, required) | Applies every edit of a preview to the open spec, in order, as one step that one undo reverts, and ends the preview. Only the person commits a preview, with Accept in Caliper: a call from an agent, from caliper-mcp or from a program is refused with preview.not_allowed. When the open spec changed since the edits were made, they are applied to it again, and when one no longer applies the commit is refused with history.conflict and nothing changes. |
| `preview_discard` | `preview.discard` | `read` | `read-only`, `frame-thread` | `id` (string, required) | Ends a preview and drops its edits. The open spec, the undo history and the journal stay as they were, as if the preview had never been made. |

## Workspace Instrument Commands

Workspace instrument commands save, open, and list spec-based instruments in the builder workspace.

| MCP Tool | Command | Effect | Flags | Arguments | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `instrument_save` | `instrument.save` | `change` | `mutates`, `destructive`, `frame-thread` | `id` (string), `manifest_id` (string), `overwrite` (boolean) | Saves the open spec as an instrument of the workspace: the folder instruments/&lt;id&gt;/ with a manifest &lt;id&gt;.caliper.toml and the spec &lt;id&gt;.spec.toml. The id is the spec's instrument id unless one is given. The manifest id, which app.launch takes, is manifest_id when given; otherwise an overwrite keeps the saved one and a new instrument gets local.&lt;id&gt;, with each _ replaced by -. Saving over an existing instrument needs overwrite set to true. It writes files, so an agent's call needs the person's approval, and it cannot be undone. |
| `instrument_open` | `instrument.open` | `change` | `mutates`, `frame-thread` | `id` (string, required) | Opens a saved instrument of the workspace by its id, from instrument.list, as the open spec, so that it can be edited. Undo returns to the spec that was open before. |
| `instrument_list` | `instrument.list` | `read` | `read-only` | None | Lists the instruments written as specs and saved in the workspace, with each one's id, title, folder and the time it was last saved. The id is what instrument.open takes. It changes nothing. |

## Provenance Review Commands

Provenance review commands report foreign spec review status for custom GPU programs.

| MCP Tool | Command | Effect | Flags | Arguments | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `review_status` | `review.status` | `read` | `read-only` | None | Says which of your commands wait for the person's approval in Caliper before they run: destructive commands, and edits of the open spec when the person reviews spec changes from your origin (for agents, on by default). A call that waits is held until the person decides, for up to 120 seconds, or answered with command.needs_approval; a dry run, an edit of a preview and an edit that changes nothing never wait. An agent that asks the person itself before a change can leave out what Caliper already asks. It changes nothing. |

## Spec Control Commands

Spec control commands create, patch, remove, and set interactive controls on the active spec.

| MCP Tool | Command | Effect | Flags | Arguments | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `control_create` | `control.create` | `edit` | `mutates`, `frame-thread` | `bind` (string), `closable` (boolean), `dry_run` (boolean), `id` (string, required), `kind` (enum, required), `options` (object), `place` (object), `title` (string) | Adds a control to the open spec: a slider, a button or a toggle that the person and you can use. bind names its one target: param:&lt;name&gt; for a parameter of the running script, action:&lt;name&gt; for an action of it, run:pause for pausing and resuming the run, value for a value the spec holds, or intervene:&lt;point&gt; for an intervention point, which a toggle ablates while it is on. run.state lists the parameters and actions, and intervene.points the points. A control is a leaf of the layout, like a panel: place puts it next to a panel or control, and without place it goes under the whole layout. Undo removes it. The result holds the change as a diff; with dry_run true the change is only checked and not applied. |

The id cannot change. The id comes from spec.get. Undo restores the control. The result holds the change as a diff; with dry_run true the change is only checked and not applied. |
| `control_remove` | `control.remove` | `edit` | `mutates`, `frame-thread` | `dry_run` (boolean), `id` (string, required) | Removes a control from the open spec and from its layout. Refuses with control.not_closable when the control sets closable to false, and with layout.locked when the layout is locked. The id comes from spec.get. Undo restores it in its place. The result holds the change as a diff; with dry_run true the change is only checked and not applied. |
| `control_set` | `control.set` | `change` | `read-only`, `frame-thread` | `id` (string, required), `value` (value, required) | Sets the value of a control that binds value or a state, as a person's edit does, and returns the value. It adds a control event with the origin of the caller. A control that binds a parameter takes run.set_param, and this command refuses it with control.not_settable. It changes the session and not the workspace, so it has no undo step. |

| `state_remove` | `state.remove` | `edit` | `mutates`, `frame-thread` | `dry_run` (boolean), `id` (string, required) | Removes a state variable from the open spec. A reference, a control or a pick that reads or writes the variable keeps it in use, and the command then fails with state.in_use. state.get lists the ids. Undo restores the variable. The result holds the change as a diff; with dry_run true the change is only checked and not applied. |
| `state_set` | `state.set` | `change` | `read-only`, `frame-thread` | `id` (string, required), `value` (value, required) | Sets the current value of a state variable, as a person's edit of a control does, and returns the value and the one before it. The value must fit the type, the bounds and the choices, or the command fails with state.bad_value. It adds a state event with the origin of the caller. It changes the session and not the workspace, so it has no undo step. |
| `state_get` | `state.get` | `read` | `read-only`, `frame-thread` | `ids` (array) | Returns the state variables of the open spec: each one's id, type, current value, default, the writers that set it and the readers that use it. ids limits the answer to some variables. It changes nothing. |

## Run Control and Managed Run Commands

Run commands inspect and steer attached scripts and start, fork, or stop managed workspace runs.

| MCP Tool | Command | Effect | Flags | Arguments | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `run_state` | `run.state` | `read` | `read-only`, `frame-thread` | `run` (string) | Returns the state of the script that the app is attached to: whether one is attached, whether the app may control it and why not, the run's state and step, its parameters with their values, ranges and pending values, and its actions. It changes nothing. |
| `run_set_param` | `run.set_param` | `run` | `frame-thread` | `name` (string, required), `run` (string), `value` (number|integer|boolean|string, required) | Sets one parameter of the running script, such as its learning rate. The value applies at the script's next step (caliper.step(), or each optimizer step under caliper.watch(model, optimizer)), and the script clamps it to the parameter's range. The result says the value is pending; a run event of change param reports the value the script applied, through events.wait. run.state lists the parameters. |
| `run_action` | `run.action` | `run` | `frame-thread` | `name` (string, required), `run` (string) | Runs one action that the running script registered with caliper.action, such as saving a checkpoint. The script runs it at its next step; the result says it is queued, and a run event of change action brings the text it returned, or its error, through events.wait. run.state lists the actions. |
| `run_pause` | `run.pause` | `run` | `frame-thread` | `count` (integer), `op` (enum, required), `run` (string) | Pauses the running script at its next step, resumes it, or lets it run a number of steps and pause again. A script pauses only at a step, so a pause before its first step is refused. The result gives the state the request was sent in; run.state and the run events of change state follow it. |
| `run_list` | `run.list` | `read` | `read-only`, `frame-thread` | None | Lists the runs: the managed runs that the model runner started, in the order of their start, and the person's own script when the app is attached to one, with the id user. Each run has its state, script, arguments, parameters, parent, step and exit code. It changes nothing. |
| `run_start` | `run.start` | `run` | `frame-thread` | `args` (array), `dictionary` (string), `id` (string), `kind` (enum), `model` (string), `params` (array), `prompt` (string), `script` (string) | Starts a managed workspace script or local inference through the fixed Caliper module. Script runs take script, args, and params, with optional kind:script. Inference runs require kind:inference, model, dictionary, and prompt. The two forms cannot mix fields. Both forms wait for approval on a review card. The result has state starting when the process starts. A runner event through events.wait, or run.list, reports later state changes. |
| `run_fork` | `run.fork` | `run` | `frame-thread` | `id` (string), `interventions` (array), `params` (array), `run` (string, required), `step` (integer) | Starts a new managed run from the next checkpoint of a running run, with changed parameters, beside its parent: the parent saves a checkpoint through its caliper.checkpoint action, and the fork runs the same script and arguments from it. It always waits for the person's approval on a review card. The result comes at once, in the state starting; a run event of change runner or run.list says when the fork runs. |
| `run_stop` | `run.stop` | `run` | `frame-thread` | `kill_after_s` (number), `run` (string, required) | Stops a managed run at its next checkpoint through its caliper.stop action, and ends its process by its id when it has not ended after kill_after_s seconds. The result comes at once, with stopping true; run.list or a run event of change runner says when the run exited. |
| `run_logs` | `run.logs` | `read` | `read-only`, `frame-thread` | `lines` (integer), `run` (string, required) | Returns the last lines that a managed run wrote to its standard output and standard error, which the runner keeps in the run's output.log. It changes nothing. |

## Event Stream Commands

Event commands wait for live run, pick, and program events from the host ring.

| MCP Tool | Command | Effect | Flags | Arguments | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `events_wait` | `events.wait` | `read` | `read-only` | `cursor` (integer), `kinds` (array), `limit` (integer), `panels` (array), `timeout_s` (number) | Returns the events that came after a cursor: picks and selections in the app's views and scene panels, changes of controls, changes of the running script (state, parameters, actions, attachment), edits of the open spec, approvals, the compile, refusal and stop of GPU programs, writes of state variables and moves of the cursor. It answers at once when events wait, and otherwise holds the call until one comes or timeout_s ends. Pass the cursor of each result to the next call. The app keeps the last 1024 events; lost counts those that were dropped before you read them. Hovers are not events. It changes nothing. |

## GPU Program Commands

Program commands attach, patch, remove, read, and inspect GPU programs and piece instances.

| MCP Tool | Command | Effect | Flags | Arguments | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `program_create` | `program.create` | `edit` | `mutates`, `frame-thread` | `bind` (value), `dry_run` (boolean), `entry` (string), `id` (string, required), `inline` (object), `inputs` (array), `limits` (object), `output` (object), `panel` (string), `params` (value), `piece` (object), `title` (string), `wgsl` (string), `workgroups` (array) | Adds a GPU program to the open spec: a WGSL compute pass that reads live tensors of the running script in place and read-only, and writes one output. A geometry output becomes an entity of a scene panel. A pixels output becomes the live view program.&lt;id&gt;, which an image panel shows through a source of catalog live:program.&lt;id&gt;. The program runs in the script's process every N steps, with N set so that training keeps 95 percent of its speed, and a program over its time or memory limit stops. The sandbox checks the declaration and the source first; a refused program is not added, and messages give the compiler's line and column. program.status reports its state. Undo removes it. With dry_run true the change is only checked and not applied. An instance of a piece takes piece, bind, panel and params in place of the WGSL keys, and inline adds a whole piece to the spec's inline pieces in the same step; a missing or changed piece is piece.missing or piece.hash_mismatch. |
| `program_patch` | `program.patch` | `edit` | `mutates`, `frame-thread` | `dry_run` (boolean), `id` (string, required), `patch` (object, required) | Changes a GPU program of the open spec with a JSON merge patch (RFC 7386) of its title, wgsl, entry, inputs, output, limits and workgroups: the keys given replace the program's own, a key set to null is removed, and output and limits merge key by key. The id cannot change. The sandbox checks the program again, and the script runs the new version from its next pass. Undo restores the program. With dry_run true the change is only checked and not applied. |
| `program_remove` | `program.remove` | `edit` | `mutates`, `frame-thread` | `dry_run` (boolean), `id` (string, required) | Removes a GPU program from the open spec; the script stops it and frees its buffers, and its output leaves the scene or the live view. The id comes from spec.get or program.status. Undo restores it. The result holds the change as a diff; with dry_run true the change is only checked and not applied. |
| `program_status` | `program.status` | `read` | `read-only`, `frame-thread` | `id` (string) | Returns the state of each GPU program of the open spec: where it runs, whether it compiled, runs, was refused or stopped, its cadence N, the GPU time of its last pass, the overhead of a pass and the base step time on the run's wall clock, the measured share of the training time, its passes a second, its memory, and its last error or active warning with line and column. It changes nothing. |
| `program_read` | `program.read` | `read` | `read-only`, `frame-thread` | `count` (integer), `first` (integer), `id` (string, required), `resource` (string, required), `step` (integer) | Reads elements of a published resource of a program at a step, as the app's step history keeps it: the step of the version, its valid count, and each element's fields as numbers. It lets an agent check what its derive half wrote. It changes nothing. |

## Session-Only Commands

Commands with `agents: false` belong to interactive user history in the desktop application.
The `caliper-mcp` server omits them from `tools/list` and refuses them for `mcp` and `agent` origins.

| Command | Effect | Flags | Arguments | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `history.undo` | `change` | `mutates`, `frame-thread` | `steps` (integer) | Undoes the most recent change to the workspace, or the given number of steps. A step is one command, several commands sent with the same group, or a run of commands merged by a merge key, such as a slider drag. Undo restores the open spec and the saved loader recipes; it does not undo saving an instrument or running a loader. Undo is the person's tool: the app's UI, the builder and programs over Caliper API may undo, and an agent may not; an agent takes back a change with an edit. history.list shows the steps first. |
| `history.redo` | `change` | `mutates`, `frame-thread` | `steps` (integer) | Redoes the step that was undone most recently, or the given number of steps. Any new change to the workspace clears what can be redone. Redo is the person's tool, as undo is: an agent may not redo. |
